title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
keyIdea: If you sell on day i, the best day to have bought is the cheapest day up to i. So walk once, keep mini = cheapest price so far, and track the best prices[i] − mini.

approaches.name: Brute force: every (buy, sell) pair
approaches.idea: For every buy day i, try every sell day j ≥ i and keep the biggest prices[j] − prices[i].
approaches.why: About n²/2 pairs. With n up to 10⁵ that's ~5·10⁹ checks: Time Limit Exceeded.

approaches.name: One pass: cheapest so far
approaches.idea: For each day: mini = min(mini, price), then profit = max(profit, price − mini). Selling today, the best buy is the lowest price seen up to today.
approaches.why: One loop, two O(1) updates per day, two int variables.

quiz.q: Selling on day i, which buy day is best?
options: The cheapest day from 0 up to i, which is exactly mini
The cheapest day in the whole array

quiz.q: Why can't you just use max(prices) − min(prices)?
options: The min might come after the max, and you can't sell before you buy
0: never trading is allowed, and profit starts at 0

quiz.q: Why is it safe to update mini before profit on the same day?
options: If today is the new low, today's profit is 0, which never beats the best
